name: open-weight models named by government evaluation bodies for cyber capability (as of November 2026)
rule: A model is listed once a government evaluation body publishes that it is the most cyber-capable open-weight model at release, or that it outperforms a model so named. Derivatives inherit the listing.

models.finding: Named the most cyber-capable open-weight model released to date.
models.source: US CAISI, Assessment of Z.ai's GLM-5.3 Cyber Capabilities, 17 September 2026

models.finding: Outperforms GLM-5.2, which the same assessment calls the most cyber-capable open-weight model as of June 2026; its safeguards did not prevent offensive cyber work in the evaluation.
models.source: UK AISI and US CAISI, Preliminary Assessment of Kimi K3's Cyber Capabilities, July 2026

models.finding: Probably the most capable open-weight model when released; its safeguards allow help with agentic exploit development, and the report notes that safeguards on open weights can be circumvented when self-hosted.
models.source: US CAISI, Assessment of Z.ai's GLM-5.2, July 2026
